correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the two polynomial modulus identities. Their quotient R=Q/P has matching zero orders at 0 and infinity and obeys R(e^{2iθ}z)=R(z). For θ=πp/q reduced, the fixed field is C(z^q), and the real-axis unit-modulus condition pairs S(w) zeros and poles by complex conjugation. Polynomial divisibility on full q-orbits is precisely -b_λ≤t_λ≤a_λ, yielding the independent product. Each nonzero orbit choice consumes ≥q roots, so ∏(a+b+1)≤2^{floor(d/q)}, with the supplied products attaining equality. Degree 2d intensity polynomials show sufficiency of 2d+1 distinct samples per line, not minimality. Checked example with nontrivial numerator p=2/3 and full zero-flip finite tests as corroboration, not universal proof.
residual_risks: Statement concerns polynomial Q under same degree cap and noiseless lines; no stability or optimal sampling count is proved. Numerical examples are not substitutes for the divisor proof.
